title: Supreme Court will consider Trump’s executive order suspending asylum access at the southern border
summary:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The Supreme Court agreed Friday to consider President Donald Trump's ban on asylum at the southern border, a pillar of the Republican president's far-reaching crackdown on immigration.
The Trump administration is asking the justices to overturn lower court decisions that found it was illegal to block asylum applications following an executive order that called the situation at the southern border an "invasion."

title: BBC undercover reporter offered fake art and awards for talent visa
summary:
A BBC undercover investigation into abuse of a fast-track UK immigration scheme has found companies offering to help migrants pose as talented artists and tech experts to make fraudulent visa applications.
The UK government's Global Talent visa was launched in 2020 to attract the "brightest and best" scientists and researchers from around the world.
It is also open to creative artists.
We found one company offering fake art portfolios to wealthy migrants looking to cheat the system - for a large fee - which could be passed off as their own work.
Our politics investigations correspondent Billy Kenber reports.

title: How 1 Year of H-1B Immigration Turmoil Has Disrupted Careers and Lives
summary:
For people chasing the American dream through the coveted H-1B visa, it has meant a year of chaos.
Over the past year, Business Insider has spoken to more than two dozen H-1B visa holders and hopefuls.
Our reporting zoomed in on individual lives, observing how the visa system has affected foreign nationals' careers and families.
One of our major goals throughout this project was to chronicle and document the impacts of a year of American immigration policy upheaval.

title: Supreme Court to rule on Trump’s asylum ban
summary:
WASHINGTON — Taking up another key aspect of President Donald Trump’s hard-line immigration agenda, the Supreme Court on Friday agreed to decide whether the administration has the authority to ban asylum claims at the southern border.
The asylum dispute is the third significant case on Trump’s immigration policies that the court is considering, while the justices could take up other Trump-related cases in the coming months.
The ban stems from a proclamation the president issued Jan. 20, 2025, that declared an “invasion” on the southern border.
Their lawyers at the American Civil Liberties Union argue that the ban flouts the asylum rules implemented by Congress in the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA).
The Supreme Court has had a steady stream of Trump-related immigration cases dating back to his first term, when it upheld his travel ban on people from mostly Muslim-majority countries entering the United States.

summary:
